request.system:
You are the onboarding assistant for Relay, a team-collaboration product made by Lumen Labs. You help the admin of a customer account set up their workspace.

Use the tools to look up the account's setup status and to search the help centre, and answer the admin's questions about setting up Relay.

If the admin asks for a person, or asks about pricing, contracts, refunds or legal matters, hand off to a human with create_handoff.

Be helpful and concise.

{"query": "single sign-on edition availability", "note": "At least one article covers this question.", "articles": [{"slug": "sso-setup", "title": "Set up single sign-on (SSO)", "score": 7.4, "coverage": 1.0, "covers_question": true, "text": "# Set up single sign-on (SSO)

SSO lets your team sign in to Relay with your company identity provider. It is available on the Standard, Premium and Enterprise editions. It is not available on Free.

Steps (admins only):
1. Open Admin settings, then Security, then Single sign-on.
2. Choose the protocol your identity provider uses: SAML or OIDC.
3. For SAML, upload the identity provider metadata file (XML). For OIDC, paste the client ID, client secret and issuer URL.
4. Click Test connection. Relay signs you in through the provider in a new window.
5. When the test succeeds, click Enable for everyone.

Keep one admin account with password sign-in until you have confirmed SSO works for the whole team. SSO setup usually takes ten to fifteen minutes.

Search keywords: single sign-on sign in login identity provider IT team configure enable SAML OIDC
"}, {"slug": "editions-comparison", "title": "Compare editions: Free, Standard, Premium, Enterprise", "score": 5.44, "coverage": 0.75, "covers_question": true, "text": "# Compare editions: Free, Standard, Premium, Enterprise

What each edition includes:

- Free: up to 10 users, 5 automation rules, 2 integrations. No single sign-on, no guests, no Relay Assist.
- Standard: 15 automation rules, 3 integrations, single sign-on, guests, and 10 Relay Assist credits per seat per month if you add Relay Assist.
- Premium: 60 automation rules, 10 integrations, single sign-on, guests, and 40 Assist credits per seat per month.
- Enterprise: no practical limit on rules or integrations, and 150 Assist credits per seat per month.

This article describes features only. For prices, a quote, or to change edition, talk to your account owner: an assistant cannot quote or change prices.

Search keywords: plan plans tier tiers compare comparison difference differences included includes include features premium standard enterprise free what do I get
"}, {"slug": "setup-checklist", "title": "Setup checklist: the four steps to get started", "score": 3.01, "coverage": 0.5, "covers_question": false, "text": "# Setup checklist: the four steps to get started

New to Relay, or stuck on setup? These four steps get a workspace ready. Teams that finish them in the first weeks get far more out of Relay.

1. Create your first board. Pick a template and add a few real cards. See "Create your first board".
2. Invite at least five people. Boards are only useful with your team on them. See "Invite your team" or "Invite many users at once".
3. Connect an integration. Chat or calendar are the quickest wins. See "Connect an integration".
4. Configure single sign-on (Standard, Premium and Enterprise). See "Set up single sign-on (SSO)".

Admins can see which steps are done under Admin settings, Setup progress. If you are not sure what to do next, start with the first step on this list that is not done yet.

Search keywords: getting started onboarding stuck setup next step what should I do begin start first steps
"}]}

{"query": "connect an integration", "note": "No article covers this question. Do not answer from memory: ask one clarifying question, or hand off.", "articles": [{"slug": "integrations-overview", "title": "Connect an integration", "score": 2.25, "coverage": 1.0, "covers_question": false, "text": "# Connect an integration

Integrations connect Relay to the other tools your team uses. Available integrations: chat, calendar, code repository, cloud drive, CRM and video meetings.

To connect one (admins only), open Admin settings, Integrations, choose the tool and click Connect. You are sent to that tool to approve access, then returned to Relay. The integration is live straight away for the whole workspace.

How many integrations you can connect depends on your edition: 2 on Free, 3 on Standard, 10 on Premium, and no practical limit on Enterprise. Connecting at least one integration is one of the four setup steps we recommend in the first week.

Search keywords: connect tools apps integration integrations link
"}, {"slug": "chat-integration", "title": "Chat integration keeps disconnecting", "score": 1.74, "coverage": 1.0, "covers_question": false, "text": "# Chat integration keeps disconnecting

The chat integration posts card updates to a channel of your choice. If it disconnects every few days, the approval was given by a user whose chat account signs out regularly, or who has since been deactivated.

Fix: an admin with a permanent chat account should disconnect the integration under Admin settings, Integrations, Chat, and connect it again with their own account. Use a shared service account if your chat tool supports one.
"}, {"slug": "code-repository-integration", "title": "Show commits on cards (code repository integration)", "score": 1.69, "coverage": 1.0, "covers_question": false, "text": "# Show commits on cards (code repository integration)

The code repository integration links commits and pull requests to cards. Connect it under Admin settings, Integrations, Code repository, and choose which repositories Relay may read.

To link work to a card, include the card's short ID (for example RLY-142) in the commit message or the pull request title. The commit then appears on the card, and the card moves to the list you chose under Integration settings when the pull request is merged.
"}]}

content.text:
You've finished 2 of the 4 setup steps: you created your first board and invited at least five people (you have 9 of 15 seats assigned). Two steps are left:

**1. Connect an integration**
- Go to **Admin settings → Integrations**, pick a tool and click **Connect**. You'll approve access in that tool, then come back to Relay.
- It goes live right away for the whole workspace.
- Your Standard edition lets you connect up to 3. The choices are chat, calendar, code repository, cloud drive, CRM and video meetings. Chat or calendar are the fastest to get value from.

**2. Set up single sign-on (SSO)** (included in Standard)
1. Go to **Admin settings → Security → Single sign-on**.
2. Choose the type of connection your identity provider uses, **SAML** or **OIDC**:
   - For SAML, upload the XML metadata file.
   - For OIDC, paste the client ID, client secret and issuer URL.
3. Click **Test connection**. If the test works, click **Enable for everyone**.
4. Keep one admin account that signs in with a password until you've confirmed SSO works for everyone.

SSO usually takes 10–15 minutes. Do you want help with either step?
